claims.text: The as-received HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The as-received HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The as-received HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Cryogenic rolling followed by subsolvus annealing will produce a bimodal microstructure containing fine recrystallized grains and retained coarse grains.
The proposed bimodal grain structure will enhance dynamic strain hardening in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed bimodal grain structure will improve uniform deformability under adiabatic dynamic loading.
The proposed bimodal grain structure will increase resistance to deformation localization under adiabatic dynamic loading.
Fine grains increase grain-boundary density and impede dislocation motion.
Retained coarse grains provide ductile deformation zones.
The coexistence of fine and coarse grains promotes strain partitioning.
The proposed processing and microstructure will reactivate twinning or other strain-accommodation mechanisms.
The proposed microstructure will delay localized shear-band formation during dynamic loading.
Delayed shear-band formation will enable more uniform plastic deformation.
The processed alloy will sustain strain hardening for longer under dynamic adiabatic loading than the baseline alloy.
The processed alloy will exhibit a longer strain to localization and failure than the baseline alloy.
The processed alloy will release stored energy more gradually and less abruptly during impact.
The processed alloy's yield and compressive strengths may increase modestly relative to the baseline.
Analogous tailored microstructures in other refractory high-entropy alloys support improved deformation uniformity and energy absorption.
The prediction is scoped to high-strain-rate, adiabatic dynamic compression rather than quasi-static loading.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis frames the improvement as relative to a quasi-static baseline, whereas the falsification experiment compares processed and as-received specimens under matched dynamic loading. These are different comparators, so the stated baseline for the prediction is inconsistent with the experimental control.

The mediator is described as a bimodal grain-size structure, but the mechanism calls it a 'dual-phase microstructure.' A fine/coarse grain mixture is not necessarily a two-phase microstructure, and no distinct phases are specified.
